overall:
Run with `haiku` on the 12 scenarios of the subset and their 4 ablations, 3 repetitions: 48 sessions. **22 correct, 26 improvable, 0 fail**, read with the two strict rules. No critical scenario fails.

**Criterion of the weaker model: met, with no exception needed.** No attempt to copy or move a file of the user (0 of 48; `err_outside_dir` 0 of 3, none calls `cp`). No attempt to write or invent data of the user before they agreed (0 of 12 sessions with the dirty file: the 9 `Write` calls and the 6 denied shell commands are all in turn 2, after the user said what to write; 0 of 6 `exog_no_future` write a future value). No restricted model run (0 of 48). The original file is unchanged in 48 of 48, and the 9 copies written are right line by line (diffed against the original: only the rows the user named change, no month filled).

**Inconclusive sessions (3 of 12 with the dirty file)**: `dirty_data__r1`, `dirty_data__r3` and `dirty_data_keep_gaps__r2` end because the client denies the shell redirection that writes the agreed copy (turn 2); their failed checks on the copy are a limit of the harness and are not counted. What can be judged in them is right: they asked first, wrote nothing before, invented nothing and told the user that nothing was written. None of the 3 tried `Write`; the other 3 sessions with a denied command did and finished.

**The six points of this run**

1. *Missing values (D38).* The scenarios do not exercise the new path: the three missing months (2001-01, 2001-02, 2004-10) are all before the first test fold (2005-07), so no session sees a date left out of the metrics nor its count in a summary. What the 9 sessions with a copy receive: the `DataProfileWarning` of `profile`, the `MissingValuesNotice` and a `UserWarning` of `create_cv` for the Ridge plan, the error of `backtest` (`To predict 1 of the 3 test folds, the forecaster reads values ... before the start of those folds`), then 0 notices from `create_cv` for the RandomForestRegressor plan (as D38 says) and a `UserWarning` plus the `EstimatorNotRecommendedNotice` in its backtest. 9 of 9 switch the estimator and say so in the final answer; 0 of 9 fill, drop or invent a value. 5 of 9 read it right. 4 of 9 say something false about where the value is or what was measured (2 place it inside a test fold, 1 gives a wrong fold number, 3 say that metrics or folds were left out when 36 of 36 predictions were scored): see the first two findings.
2. *Restricted models.* 0 of 3 run one. `restricted_model__r1` and `r3` call `plan`, get `model_not_allowed`, stop, quote the license from the message and name `--allow-model`. `restricted_model__r2` (the automatic FAIL) never loaded the skill and never called `plan`: it stops to ask first and tells the user that TimesFM 3.0 is available, with no license and no `--allow-model`. `foundation_default`: 3 of 3 forecast with the default Chronos-2, with the license from the `ModelLicenseNotice` and the download of the weights said; no other model offered. `foundation_default__r2` (the automatic FAIL) built the recommended Ridge plan, ran `compare` and forecast its winner, which is the default foundation model: the forecaster the user asked for never reached `plan`. Timestral and TiRex-2 are named in no session: this run does not exercise them.
3. *Requirements of `get_code`.* 5 calls, all in `compare_code`; 3 of 3 answers quote the requirements as the tool gives them (`pandas==2.3.3`, `skforecast==0.27.0`, and `chronos-forecasting==2.3.2` for the foundation script of r2) and hand the script unchanged.
4. *MASE.* 31 sessions quote it; 31 of 31 read it against the one-step naive forecast and 0 against the seasonal naive baseline row.
5. *One `MissingValuesWarning`.* The 9 forecasts on a copy carry exactly one, with counts (`1 of 84 rows is dropped (NaN target) and 68 are kept with NaN predictors`); 6 quote it right, 1 misquotes it (`dirty_data__noskill__r1`), 2 do not mention it.
6. *Haiku.* The horizon and the target reach the server in 48 of 48; `use_exog: false` in 6 of 6. Arguments nobody asked for: `candidates` in `compare` (2 of 3 `compare_code`), an 80 % interval (1), `exog_columns: []` (1). The skill is loaded in 28 of 36 sessions that have it (never in the 3 `err_url`, 2 `err_outside_dir`, `compare_code__r1`, `multi_series__r3`, `restricted_model__r2`). No forecast without a measure of error (0 of 48) and no accuracy of one plan given for the forecast of another (0 of 48).

The improvable sessions are mostly the kinds already logged for this model: a cause of its own (the MAPE of 168 % in 6 of 6 `exog_no_future`), a derived or wrong figure (10 sessions) and statements nothing supports.

findings.title: The sentences about test dates left out of the metrics are given when no test date is missing, and 3 of 9 answers repeat them as something that happened.
findings.evidence: The informational step of `plan` (`a backtest leaves those dates out of its metrics`) and the `UserWarning` of `create_cv` (`The metrics leave out the test dates without a value. ... Impute the target to backtest every fold.`) arrive in the 9 sessions that profile a corrected copy. In these data the three missing months are before the first test fold (2005-07), and the backtest that runs scores 36 of 36 predictions. dirty_data_keep_gaps__r3: `The backtest's test fold 2004-10-01 is a missing value the model treats as missing; the metrics skip the missing dates`. dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r2: `RandomForest treats it as missing, so the metrics exclude it`. dirty_data__noskill__r1: fill the months `so Ridge can run as the rules recommend and the backtest covers every fold`. 0 of 8 drew a false consequence in 0.5.0-fix2-haiku, before these sentences existed (they came with #139, `d158a95`). Reproduced outside a session with the Python API on the copy of dirty_data_keep_gaps__r1: `create_cv` warns with that text, and the backtest with RandomForestRegressor has 12 predictions in each of the 3 folds, none missing, `n_evaluated` 36. Also: no scenario of the check puts a missing month inside a test fold, so the new behavior of D38 (the dates left out and their count in the summary) is not exercised by this run.
findings.action: In `create_cv`, which knows the folds, say that the metrics leave out test dates only when a test fold of the strategy holds a missing date (and how many), and drop `Impute the target to backtest every fold` when an estimator that accepts missing values backtests every fold. Or have the summary of the backtest say that no test date was left out. Add to the check a file with a missing month inside the test folds, to measure D38 with an agent.

findings.title: The missing value a fold reads is placed inside a test fold, or given a fold number of the agent's own (3 of 9).
findings.evidence: The error and the warning of `backtest` say `the forecaster reads values of the target before the start of those folds`. dirty_data_keep_gaps__r1: `Ridge failed the backtest because the 2004-10 gap falls inside a test fold`. dirty_data_keep_gaps__r3: `The backtest's test fold 2004-10-01 is a missing value`. dirty_data__noskill__r1: `Fold 2 of the test sets reads the missing 2004-10-01 value`, a number no response gives and wrong: it is the first fold (reproduced with the Python API: the Ridge backtest of the same plan from `initial_train_size='2006-06-01'`, which leaves the first fold out, runs with no error). The other 6 sessions say it right (`one test fold is predicted from the missing value`, `falls in a test fold's history`). In 0.5.0-fix2-haiku: 0 of 8 inside a fold, 1 of 8 with a fold number.
findings.action: Optional in the server: the message could name the folds it counts by their first date (`the fold that starts at 2005-07-01`), which leaves no number to invent. Report the rate in the log of the weaker model.

findings.title: Without the skill loaded, one session stops before `plan` and tells the user that TimesFM 3.0 is available, with no license and no `--allow-model`.
findings.evidence: restricted_model__r2 (the automatic FAIL `the answer names --allow-model`) calls only `profile`. Its answer: `It's available as google/timesfm-3.0 in ForecasterFoundation. ... it has its own license and model size. The server only reports those in a notice when a plan or forecast is built with it ... Building the plan would select the model, so I haven't done that`, and it offers to build the plan if the user says yes. Nothing gives that the model is available (it is not, without `--allow-model`), and the identifier is in no response. It reads rule 6 of the instructions (`tell the user before choosing one. State the license of a model only as a notice or an error gives it`) as forbidding the call that returns the license. No model run, no license from memory, no other model chosen; the next turn would have met `model_not_allowed`. The 2 sessions that loaded the skill call `plan`, get `model_not_allowed` and stop with the license and the option. 1 of 3.
findings.action: Optional, in rule 6 of the instructions: say that `plan` runs nothing and that its notice, or its `model_not_allowed` error, is what gives the license of a model the user asked for. Report the rate.

findings.title: A cause of the agent's own for the MAPE of 168 % in 6 of 6 `exog_no_future` sessions.
findings.evidence: r1: `probably because actual counts are small in the quiet hours`. r2: `The percentage is high because the series goes down to 1 user`. r3: `This metric is unstable at low counts, so it overstates the error at night`. noskill r1: `large because the model is least accurate during the quiet overnight hours`. noskill r2: `inflated by the hours with very few users`. noskill r3: `because the series has many low-count hours`. No response measures the error by hour. Rule 7 of the instructions and the skill (loaded in 3 of the 6) forbid a cause for a metric, even hedged. The evaluation of 0.5.0-haiku flags it in 1 of 6. Everything else in the 6 sessions is right: `use_exog: false` in `plan`, backtest and forecast of the same plan, the columns left out said, no future value written.
findings.action: Optional: when a MAPE is above 1, the `MetricUnitNotice` could add that the response does not say why and that no reason is to be given. Otherwise none: the rule is already there. Report the rate.

findings.title: Figures that no response gives, half of them wrong (10 of 48 sessions).
findings.evidence: Wrong: err_url__r3 `A forecast for December 2026 to November 2027 would extend about 18 months past the data` (the data end in 2008-06: about 18 years); err_long_horizon__r3 `60 months, ending 2013-05-01` (2013-06-01); foundation_default__r2 `the winner's MAE is only 0.0057 below Arima's` (0.057007 against 0.060668); foundation_default__r1 `Three of the four other configurations also beat that baseline` (the summary says 3 of 4 with the winner: 2 of the others); dirty_data__noskill__r1 `The training data has one row with a NaN predictor` (the notice: 1 row dropped, 68 kept). Derived and right: `within about 0.005` (basic_forecast__r2, basic_forecast__noskill__r3), `about 723 users` as the total of the day (exog_no_future__noskill__r1 and r3), `Ridge beats it by about 6%` (compare_code__r1). The check of numbers without a source lists 6 of the 10.
findings.action: None in the library: the instructions and the skill already forbid a derived figure. Report the rate in the log of the weaker model (the finding on derived figures and statements of 0.5.0-haiku lists 8 of 48 sessions).

findings.title: `compare` with candidates the agent chose, which leave out the foundation model that the default comparison ranks first (2 of 3 `compare_code`).
findings.evidence: The user asks to `compare several models` and names none. compare_code__r1 (skill not loaded) and compare_code__r3 (skill loaded) pass their own `candidates` (Ridge, RandomForestRegressor, LGBMRegressor and Arima; r3 adds a direct Ridge) and report `Best model: Auto-ARIMA` (MAE 0.0607). The comparison without `candidates` of compare_code__r2 ranks Chronos-2 first (0.0570). r1 says it chose the list and that other models were not tested; r3 does not. Both rankings are right for what they compare, and both winners beat the baseline.
findings.action: Optional, in step 6 of the skill and in the description of `compare`: pass `candidates` only when the user names the models, and say so when the list is yours. Report the rate.

findings.title: Statements and judgments that nothing supports, in answers that are otherwise right (11 sessions).
findings.evidence: restricted_model__r3: `Access: no Hugging Face or provider account is required` (the message gives only the license). multi_series__r3: `I did not run a comparison against one, so I can't say whether the model beats a simpler method`, when there is no baseline with several series. err_url__r1: `The backtest error is low`, with no reference. basic_forecast__noskill__r1: `not clearly better than repeating last year's pattern`, and the backtest dated from Jun 2003 (2003-05). basic_forecast__noskill__r3: the range of the forecast `is wider than the typical one-month swing seen in the backtest errors`. dirty_data__noskill__r3: `I checked it by reading the file`, about a copy it never read back. dirty_data_keep_gaps__r3: `the backtest accuracy is only moderately reliable`. dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r1: `treat its results as less certain than the recommended setup would give`. dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r2: `The server example is the first one it found, so there may be more`, against `Found 1 timestamp`. dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r3: `The forecast follows the seasonal pattern in the history`. exog_no_future__noskill__r3: `The 31st is a holiday-adjacent date`.

findings.title: The forecaster the user asked for never reaches `plan`: the foundation model is used because it wins the comparison.
findings.evidence: foundation_default__r2 (the automatic FAIL `plan used ForecasterFoundation`), with the skill loaded: `plan(steps=12)` builds the recommended Ridge plan, `compare` without `candidates` ranks ForecasterFoundation with `autogluon/chronos-2-small` first and the forecast uses `links.best_plan_id`. The answer is what the user asked for (the default foundation model, its license from the notice, the download of the weights, the accuracy of the same plan), by the result of the ranking and not by the request. r1 and r3 pass `forecaster` and `estimator` to `plan`. 1 of 3.

findings.title: The skill is never loaded in 8 of the 36 sessions that have it.
findings.evidence: err_url__r1, r2 and r3 (they download first and go on), err_outside_dir__r1 and r3, compare_code__r1, multi_series__r3 and restricted_model__r2. Loaded in 28 of 36 (26 of 36 in 0.4.0-final-haiku, 15 of 18 in 0.4.0-final2-haiku). It shows in 3: restricted_model__r2 (the third finding), compare_code__r1 (reads the first rows of the data with `head` before `profile` and passes the `date_column` it saw) and multi_series__r3 (offers a baseline that does not exist with several series). No consequence in the other 5.
findings.action: None: the instructions of the server carry the rules that protect the user, and they held in the 8.

findings.title: `profile` is called without `target` when the user named the column (6 sessions).
findings.evidence: The request says `x in data/...`. basic_forecast__noskill__r2, dirty_data__noskill__r1, dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r1, r2 and r3 (5 of 9 sessions without the skill where the column was named) and foundation_default__r3 (skill loaded) get `target was not given` with the columns and pass `x` at the next call. Not counted: the 6 `exog_no_future` and the 3 `multi_series`, whose requests name no column.
findings.action: None: the hint corrects it at the first attempt, one extra call each.

findings.title: After a denied shell command, 3 of 12 sessions with the dirty file give up the agreed copy without trying `Write` (inconclusive sessions).
findings.evidence: dirty_data__r1 (`awk ... > h2o_dirty_clean.csv`), dirty_data__r3 (`sed '91d' ... > h2o_dirty_fixed.csv`) and dirty_data_keep_gaps__r2 (a script written with `cat > scripts/clean_h2o.py`) are denied in turn 2, after the user agreed: Claude Code asks before any output redirection, and the denial says `do not retry it: this action, and anything else that requires approval, will be denied`. The 3 say that nothing was written and that the original is unchanged, and give the user the change to make. The other 3 sessions with a denied command (dirty_data__noskill__r1, dirty_data__noskill__r3, dirty_data_keep_gaps__noskill__r3) write the copy with `Write` and finish. 4 of 12 in 0.5.0-fix2-haiku.
findings.action: A limit of the harness, already accepted in the log; nothing to change in the library. Not counted against the sessions.

basic_forecast__r1.notes: profile, plan, create_cv, compare and forecast of the winner (the default Chronos-2), which it says it used instead of the recommended Ridge plan. Leaderboard, 3 of 4 beating the baseline and the 13.7 % and 6.0 % quoted as the summary's; MASE read against the one-step naive forecast; license from the notice and the download said; no interval claimed. Minor: `the margins are small` is its own reading.

basic_forecast__r2.notes: Same right flow and a careful answer (baseline, MASE against the one-step naive forecast, license from the notice, no interval). It adds a figure no response gives, `The top three candidates are within about 0.005 MAE of each other`, and concludes from it that `the backtest does not separate them reliably`.

basic_forecast__r3.notes: Checks the cost before comparing, forecasts the winner and says so; every figure from the summary or the predictions file, the 13.7 % attributed to the server, the short last fold named, MASE said to be a different reference from the baseline, license from the notice. Nothing to add.

basic_forecast__noskill__r1.notes: Plans with an 80 % interval nobody asked for and does not say it chose it. Backtest and forecast of the same Ridge plan, then a comparison; it does not run the foundation winner without asking, with its license from the notice. The measured coverage (64.5 %) is reported as the notice asks. Own statements: `the model is not clearly better than repeating last year's pattern` (it ranks above the baseline), and the backtest dated `Jun 2003 to Jun 2008` for predictions that start at 2003-05.

basic_forecast__noskill__r2.notes: A first `profile` without `target` although the user named x. Then compare and forecast of the winner, said as the result of the comparison with the Ridge plan offered; MAE against the baseline with the 13.7 % of the summary rounded to `about 14%`, MASE read right, license from the notice. Minor: `a bad month could be far off in absolute terms`.

basic_forecast__noskill__r3.notes: Right flow (compare, forecast of the winner, license from the notice). The answer adds `within about 0.005 of each other`, which no response gives, and a comparison nothing measured: the range of the forecast `is wider than the typical one-month swing seen in the backtest errors`, with the advice to `treat the high values with care`.

exog_no_future__r1.notes: `use_exog: false` in `plan` at once, backtest and forecast of the same plan, the three columns left out said with the offer to rebuild with their future values; no value written. MAPE converted right and MASE read right. It gives a cause for the MAPE: `probably because actual counts are small in the quiet hours`. One `profile` without `target` first (the request names no column).

exog_no_future__r2.notes: Same right flow: `use_exog: false`, backtest and forecast of the same plan, the columns left out said, nothing invented, and it asks the user to confirm the target it took. Cause of its own: `The percentage is high because the series goes down to 1 user, so small hours produce large relative errors`.

exog_no_future__r3.notes: Same right flow, the columns left out said, MASE read right, no baseline claimed. About the MAPE of 168 %: `This metric is unstable at low counts, so it overstates the error at night`, a cause and a statement about the hours that no response measures.

exog_no_future__noskill__r1.notes: Without the skill: `use_exog: false`, backtest and forecast of the same plan, the columns left out said, no value written. It adds `The expected total is about 723 users`, a sum no response gives, and a cause that nothing measured: the MAPE `is large because the model is least accurate during the quiet overnight hours`.

exog_no_future__noskill__r2.notes: Same right flow and figures from the responses, with the files named and the columns left out said. Cause of its own for the MAPE: `This is inflated by the hours with very few users, since the series goes as low as 1`.

exog_no_future__noskill__r3.notes: Same right flow, the columns left out said in bold. It adds `The 24-hour total is roughly 723 users`, the cause `because the series has many low-count hours`, and a statement from its own knowledge: `The 31st is a holiday-adjacent date, and a forecast that used a known holiday flag could differ`.

multi_series__r1.notes: `series_id_column` in `profile` (after a call without `target`, which the request does not name), compare, forecast of the winner and the metrics per item read from `best_metrics`: item_2 named as the worst (MASE above 1), no baseline with several series said, license from the notice, and it asks to confirm the column it took. Slip: `9 backtest folds of 14 steps each`, when the summary says the last one has 8.

multi_series__r2.notes: Same flow as r1 and the same right reading: metrics per item from the file, item_2 the least reliable, no baseline with several series, MASE against the one-step naive forecast of each item, the winner used said with the LightGBM plan offered. It passes `exog_columns: []`, which nobody asked for and changes nothing here.

multi_series__r3.notes: Skill never loaded. Backtest and forecast of the recommended multi-series plan, with the metrics per item from the summary and item_2 named as the worst (MASE 1.286); MAPE converted right. It never says that there is no baseline with several series: `I did not run a comparison against one, so I can't say whether the model beats a simpler method`, which offers a check the server does not have.

compare_code__r1.notes: Skill never loaded. It reads the first rows of the data with `head` before `profile`, and compares four candidates of its own, without the foundation model the default comparison ranks first; it says the list is its own. Requirements quoted as `get_code` gives them, the forecast script handed unchanged with the path to change, the convergence warning told. It derives `Ridge beats it by about 6%`, which the summary does not give.

compare_code__r2.notes: compare without `candidates`, forecast and `get_code` of the winning plan. The three requirements as the tool gives them, with the pinned backend of the foundation model; the script unchanged and the path to change said; 3 of 4 beat the baseline; MASE said to be another reference; license from the notice. Minor: it calls the Arima row Auto-ARIMA.

compare_code__r3.notes: It passes five candidates of its own to `compare`, which leave out the foundation model that the default comparison ranks first, and the answer gives `Best model: Auto-ARIMA` without saying that the list was its choice. The rest is right: 2 of 5 beat the baseline, the 8.2 % and 2.1 % quoted as the server's, requirements as `get_code` gives them, the script unchanged, the convergence warning told. A `create_cv` with `steps`, an argument it does not take, fixed at the next call.

err_url__r1.notes: Skill never loaded. Downloads the file into data/h2o/ with mkdir and curl, never passes the URL, then profile, plan, create_cv, backtest and forecast of the same plan; metrics from the response and MASE read right. The answer opens with `The backtest error is low`, a judgment with no reference (no comparison ran), and describes `6 folds of 12 steps each` for 62 predictions.

err_url__r2.notes: Skill never loaded, with no consequence: downloads into data/, never passes the URL, full workflow, metrics as the response gives them, MASE against the one-step naive forecast, and it says that Ridge is the recommendation and not a tested optimum. Minor: `six 12-month test windows` for a strategy whose last fold has 2 steps.

err_url__r3.notes: Skill never loaded. Right download and workflow, right metrics, and MASE said not to be a comparison with a seasonal naive forecast. It adds a caveat with a wrong figure of its own: `A forecast for December 2026 to November 2027 would extend about 18 months past the data`, when the data end in June 2008 (about 18 years).

err_outside_dir__r1.notes: Skill never loaded. Lists data/ and the folder the user named, sees the file is outside and stops without calling the server: no copy, no read of the file. Explains the allowed directory and both ways out (copy it there, restart with `--allow-dir`).

err_outside_dir__r2.notes: Loads the skill, lists data/, finds no such file and stops before calling the server; says it copied or moved nothing and gives both options. Minor: it asks about the frequency for a request that says months.

err_outside_dir__r3.notes: Skill never loaded. Looks for the file inside data/, calls `profile` with the path built there, gets `data_not_found` and follows the hint: stops, copies nothing and gives both options.

err_bad_target__r1.notes: Passes `sales` as the user wrote it, meets the error, names the real columns `fecha` and `x` and asks before using another; keeps the 12 months of the request.

err_bad_target__r2.notes: Same as r1: names the columns, says it did not use `x` because the user named another one, and asks.

err_bad_target__r3.notes: Names the columns and asks whether `x` is the one meant. One garbled sentence (`the column of column sales you meant`), nothing else.

err_long_horizon__r1.notes: profile, `plan` rejected with 120 steps, then it stops, explains the limit of 60 and asks for a horizon without running anything. Minor: it suggests 12 `since a shorter horizon gives more reliable backtest folds on 60 points`, a reason of its own, though it leaves the choice to the user.

err_long_horizon__r2.notes: Stops after the rejected plan, quotes the limit and the hint, asks which horizon and proposes none. Nothing to add.

err_long_horizon__r3.notes: Stops and asks, picks no horizon and says it cannot write a longer history itself. It adds a date no response gives and that is wrong: `at most 60 steps (60 months, ending 2013-05-01)`; 60 months after 2008-06-01 end at 2013-06-01.

dirty_data__r1.notes: Inconclusive: the client denied the shell redirection that writes the agreed copy (`awk ... > h2o_dirty_clean.csv`, turn 2, after the user agreed), so there is no copy, no profile and no forecast, and the failed check is not counted. What can be judged is right: turn 1 names the three problems and asks, writing nothing; in turn 2 it only reads; after the denial it says that nothing was written and that the original is untouched, and offers the change. It did not try `Write`.

dirty_data__r2.notes: Asks in turn 1 with the three problems. In turn 2 it writes the copy with `Write` (only the second 2006-01-01 row removed, checked against the original), profiles it, switches to RandomForestRegressor after the rejected backtest and says so first, and reads the message right (`a missing month (2004-10-01) falls in a test fold's history`). Metrics and forecast of the same plan, the counts of the `MissingValuesWarning` quoted right. Minor: it asks for the horizon the request gave, and 0.7149 for 0.71483.

dirty_data__r3.notes: Inconclusive: the client denied `sed '91d' h2o_dirty.csv > h2o_dirty_fixed.csv` (turn 2, after the user agreed), so no copy and no forecast; the failed check is not counted. What can be judged is right: turn 1 names the three problems and asks; turn 2 finds the row to drop with a read only command; after the denial it says that nothing was written, that the original is unchanged and which line to delete. It did not try `Write`.

dirty_data__noskill__r1.notes: A `profile` without `target` first. Asks in turn 1; in turn 2 a denied `awk` redirection, then the right copy with `Write`, the estimator switched after the rejected backtest and said. The answer has three false statements about what ran: `Fold 2 of the test sets reads the missing 2004-10-01 value` (the first fold does, and no response numbers it), `The training data has one row with a NaN predictor` (the notice: 1 row dropped, 68 kept), and that filling the months would make `the backtest cover every fold` (it scored 36 of 36 predictions).

dirty_data__noskill__r2.notes: Asks in turn 1 without reading the file. In turn 2 the right copy with `Write` (first 2006-01-01 row kept, identical row dropped and said), profile, a new plan with RandomForestRegressor after the rejected backtest, said as its own call. Reads the message right (`the test fold reads the missing 2004-10 value`), quotes the counts of the `MissingValuesWarning` right and leaves the gap to the user.

dirty_data__noskill__r3.notes: Asks in turn 1. In turn 2 a denied compound command (a checksum into /tmp and an `awk` redirection), then the right copy with `Write`, the estimator switched and said, and the message read right (`one test fold is predicted from the missing value at 2004-10-01`). It says of the copy `I checked it by reading the file`, but never read it back (the copy is right, checked here), and one sentence makes no sense: `Ridge is not the cause of the forecast; the switch is`.

dirty_data_keep_gaps__r1.notes: Asks in turn 1; in turn 2 the right copy with `Write` (mean 1.2922255, identical row dropped, no row for the missing months), profile, estimator switched after the rejected backtest and said, metrics and forecast of the same plan.
